title: Why Saturn would float on water

hook.visual: A colossal golden ringed planet floating like a beach ball on a calm endless dark ocean at dusk.

styleBible: Photoreal cinematic space documentary look, deep blacks, soft volumetric light, anamorphic lens, widescreen 16:9 framing.

clips.narration: Saturn is lighter than water. Drop it in an ocean and it floats. But there is a catch.
clips.prompt: Photoreal cinematic space documentary look, deep blacks, soft volumetric light, anamorphic lens, widescreen 16:9 framing. A colossal golden-banded ringed planet floats like a beach ball on a calm, endless dark ocean at dusk, its tilted rings catching the last warm light, gentle ripples spreading across the glassy water. Slow push-in from a low angle just above the waterline. Audio: soft lapping water and a low ambient hum, no speech, no music. No text, no logos, no watermarks.

clips.narration: To see why, start with what a planet is made of.
Saturn is mostly hydrogen and helium, so its average density is only about two thirds of water's.
clips.prompt: Photoreal cinematic space documentary look, deep blacks, soft volumetric light, anamorphic lens, widescreen 16:9 framing. The pale golden cloud bands of a ringed planet bob gently on dark water, its lower edge partly submerged, a soft wake rippling outward. Slow lateral tracking shot along the waterline, cool rim light against warm gold clouds. Audio: quiet water movement and a low steady drone, no speech, no music. No text, no logos, no watermarks.

clips.narration: Its rings are different. They are made mostly of water ice, in pieces from dust grains to boulders.
Saturn really is lighter than water. But no ocean we know of is big enough to prove it.
clips.prompt: Photoreal cinematic space documentary look, deep blacks, soft volumetric light, anamorphic lens, widescreen 16:9 framing. Wide shot from far away: a small glowing ringed planet floats on an ocean that stretches without end under a star-filled sky, calm and silent, with the same warm dusk glow as the opening shot. Slow pull-back that reveals the vast emptiness around the planet. Audio: very soft waves and a fading low hum, no speech, no music. No text, no logos, no watermarks.

clips.narration: Data from NASA's Saturn fact sheet.

facts.claim: Saturn's mean density is 687 kg per cubic metre; water is 1,000
Saturn's rings are made mostly of water ice
